region: North America north of central Mexico (incl. Greenland and northern Mexico)

polities.name: Haudenosaunee Confederacy
polities.note: Founding date debated (c.1142–1450); 1450 used. Five Nations, Tuscarora joined 1722. Beaver Wars hunting-ground reach 1650–1701; land ceded 1784–1797, then reservations in NY and Six Nations of the Grand River (Ontario).

polities.name: Mohawk
polities.note: Eastern door of the Confederacy; most moved to Kahnawake (1667+), Akwesasne, Grand River and Tyendinaga after 1777.

polities.name: Oneida
polities.note: Most land sold to New York 1785–1838; main body removed to Green Bay, Wisconsin (Duck Creek) 1820s–1838.

polities.name: Onondaga
polities.note: Central fire-keepers of the Confederacy; reduced to the Onondaga Reservation after 1788.

polities.name: Cayuga
polities.note: Homeland lost after Sullivan Expedition (1779) and 1795 cessions; dispersed to Grand River, Buffalo Creek and Sandusky (Ohio).

polities.name: Seneca
polities.note: Western door; expanded west after destroying the Erie (1650s); Ganondagan burned 1687, later Genesee Castle; after Big Tree Treaty 1797 confined to Allegany, Cattaraugus, Tonawanda, Buffalo Creek reservations.

polities.name: Tuscarora
polities.note: Iroquoian nation of the North Carolina inner coastal plain; defeated in the Tuscarora War 1711–1713 (Neoheroka), migrated north and joined the Haudenosaunee 1722 as sixth nation.

polities.name: Wendat Confederacy
polities.note: Four (later five) nations; before c.1550 villages lay on the north shore of Lake Ontario (Toronto–Rice Lake), then concentrated in Huronia between Georgian Bay and Lake Simcoe. Dispersed by the Haudenosaunee 1649–50; remnants to Wendake (Quebec) and the Wyandot.

polities.name: Wendake (Huron-Wendat of Lorette)
polities.note: Refugee Wendat community near Quebec City under French/British protection.

polities.name: Wyandot
polities.note: Successors of the Petun and Huron refugees; at Michilimackinac 1670s, Detroit 1701, Sandusky region from c.1740; removed to Kansas 1843 and Indian Territory 1867.

polities.name: Petun
polities.note: Iroquoian nation west of Huronia (Blue Mountains); dispersed 1649–50, merged into the Wyandot.

polities.name: Neutral Confederacy
polities.note: Iroquoian confederacy of the Niagara Peninsula and Grand River; destroyed by the Haudenosaunee 1650–51.

polities.name: Erie
polities.note: SE shore of Lake Erie between the Buffalo River and Presque Isle Bay; influence perhaps onto the Allegheny Plateau. Capital Rigué's location uncertain. Destroyed by Seneca/Onondaga 1654–56.

polities.name: Wenro
polities.note: Small Iroquoian people east of the Erie; fled to Huronia 1639.

polities.name: St. Lawrence Iroquoians
polities.note: Village chiefdoms along the St Lawrence (Stadacona, Hochelaga) met by Cartier 1535; disappeared c.1580, probably through warfare.

polities.name: Susquehannock
polities.note: Upper Susquehanna (Bradford Co., PA) until c.1575, then lower Susquehanna; broken by war 1675; remnant Conestoga town until the 1763 Paxton massacre.

polities.name: Lenape
polities.note: Lenapehoking (Delaware valley, NJ, lower Hudson) until 1740s Walking Purchase; then Susquehanna/Allegheny, Muskingum (Ohio) 1765–1794, White River (Indiana) 1795–1820, Kansas 1830–1867, Cherokee Nation (Indian Territory) 1867.

polities.name: Mahican
polities.note: Upper Hudson valley; pushed east by Mohawk (1628); Stockbridge mission 1734; New Stockbridge NY 1785; Wisconsin from 1822.

polities.name: Wappinger
polities.note: Munsee-speaking bands on the east bank of the lower Hudson; broken by Kieft's War (1643–45); remnants merged with the Stockbridge.

polities.name: Wampanoag
polities.note: Sachemship of Massasoit and Metacom over SE Massachusetts, Cape Cod and islands; broken in King Philip's War 1675–76; island/Mashpee communities persisted.

polities.name: Narragansett
polities.note: Dominant power of Rhode Island west of Narragansett Bay; defeated in the Great Swamp Fight 1675; later small Charlestown reservation.

polities.name: Pequot
polities.note: Dominant southern New England power c.1620–1636; destroyed in the Pequot War 1636–38 (Treaty of Hartford).

polities.name: Mohegan
polities.note: Split from the Pequot under Uncas; English ally; reduced to a reserve by the early 18th c.

polities.name: Massachusett
polities.note: Sachemdoms around Massachusetts Bay; devastated by the 1616–19 epidemic; absorbed into praying towns by 1650.

polities.name: Nipmuc
polities.note: Inland bands of central Massachusetts; partly tributary to Narragansett/Wampanoag; broken in King Philip's War.

polities.name: Pocumtuck
polities.note: Middle Connecticut River confederacy; defeated by the Mohawk 1664–67.

polities.name: Pennacook
polities.note: Merrimack valley confederacy under Passaconaway; withdrew north to Odanak and Schaghticoke c.1690–1700.

polities.name: Western Abenaki
polities.note: Vermont, New Hampshire and upper Connecticut valley; refugee centres at Odanak (St-François) and Bécancour from c.1700; Vermont homeland largely lost by c.1800.

polities.name: Eastern Abenaki
polities.note: Kennebec/Androscoggin/Saco valleys of Maine; Norridgewock destroyed 1724 (Dummer's War); survivors to Odanak and Penobscot.

polities.name: Penobscot
polities.note: Penobscot River valley; Wabanaki Confederacy member; most land ceded to Massachusetts/Maine 1796–1833, reservation islands retained.

polities.name: Passamaquoddy
polities.note: St Croix River and Passamaquoddy Bay; Wabanaki member; reservation at Pleasant Point and Indian Township from 1794.

polities.name: Wolastoqiyik
polities.note: St John River valley; Wabanaki member; Aukpaque (near Fredericton) became the main village in the 18th c.; reserves after Loyalist settlement (1783).

polities.name: Mi'kmaq
polities.note: Seven districts of Mi'kma'ki (Nova Scotia, PEI, eastern New Brunswick, Gaspé) under the Grand Council; Peace and Friendship Treaties 1725–1779; confined to reserves by the mid-19th c.; southern Newfoundland settled from the 18th c.

polities.name: Wabanaki Confederacy
polities.note: Alliance of Abenaki, Penobscot, Passamaquoddy, Wolastoqiyik and Mi'kmaq formed against Haudenosaunee and English pressure c.1680; council fire later at Kahnawake; formally dissolved 1862. Overlaps member territories.

polities.name: Beothuk
polities.note: Island of Newfoundland; pushed off the coasts by European fishermen and Mi'kmaq after c.1700, confined to the Exploits River interior; extinct 1829 (Shanawdithit).

polities.name: Innu
polities.note: Bands of the Quebec–Labrador peninsula (Nitassinan), incl. the northern Naskapi; Tadoussac trading rendezvous; no central government.

polities.name: Algonquin
polities.note: Ottawa River valley bands; Kichesipirini controlled river toll at Allumette/Morrison Island until the 1650 Haudenosaunee wars; later Kanesatake and Kitigan Zibi (1853).

polities.name: Atikamekw
polities.note: Upper Saint-Maurice River basin; Algonquian hunting bands.

polities.name: Powhatan Paramount Chiefdom
polities.note: Built by Wahunsenacawh from c.1570s over ~30 tidewater Virginia chiefdoms; seat moved to Orapax 1609; Anglo-Powhatan wars 1610–1646; tributary to Virginia from 1646; Treaty of Middle Plantation 1677.

polities.name: Piscataway
polities.note: Paramount chiefdom (tayac) of southern Maryland north of the Potomac; left Maryland 1697–1700 for Virginia and later Pennsylvania/New York.

polities.name: Nanticoke
polities.note: Chesapeake Eastern Shore chiefdom; most migrated north to the Susquehanna and the Haudenosaunee after 1748.

polities.name: Secotan and Carolina Algonquians
polities.note: Chiefdoms of the Albemarle/Pamlico sounds (Secotan, Roanoke, Chowanoke, Weapemeoc) met by the Roanoke colonists 1584–90; decimated by the 1670s.

polities.name: Monacan
polities.note: Siouan confederacy of the Virginia Piedmont (upper James and Rappahannock incl. Manahoac); dispersed early 18th c.; a remnant remained at Bear Mountain.

polities.name: Vermont Republic
polities.note: Self-governing unrecognised republic (NH Grants) from 1777 until admission to the United States 1791; legislature met in rotating towns.

polities.name: Ojibwe
polities.note: Band-based nation (part of the Council of Three Fires with Odawa and Potawatomi). Centre at Bawating, then Chequamegon/La Pointe after c.1680; expanded west and south against the Dakota through the 18th c. (Leech Lake, Red Lake, Saulteaux onto the plains). Treaties 1837–1867 (US) and Robinson 1850 / Numbered Treaties (Canada) confined bands to reservations and reserves.

polities.name: Odawa
polities.note: Manitoulin Island and Bruce Peninsula before 1650; refugees at Green Bay/Chequamegon/Michilimackinac after the Beaver Wars; Detroit from 1701 (Pontiac); northern Lower Michigan (L'Arbre Croche) from 1742; ceded land 1836 (Treaty of Washington); Manitoulin reserve and Michigan bands after.

polities.name: Potawatomi
polities.note: Southwestern Lower Michigan before c.1641; refuge on the Door Peninsula/Green Bay 1641–1700; expanded around southern Lake Michigan (St Joseph, Chicago, Milwaukee, northern Indiana) in the 18th c.; removed after the 1833 Treaty of Chicago to Iowa and Kansas.

polities.name: Ho-Chunk
polities.note: Siouan nation of the Green Bay region; spread over the Wisconsin and Rock river valleys in the 18th c.; ceded Wisconsin lands 1829–1837; removed to Iowa, Minnesota, Dakota and Nebraska (1865); many returned to Wisconsin.

polities.name: Menominee
polities.note: Algonquian nation west of Green Bay; ceded most land 1831–1848; Keshena (Wolf River) reservation from 1854.

polities.name: Meskwaki
polities.note: Probably in eastern Michigan before the Beaver Wars; on the Fox River of Wisconsin c.1660–1735 (Fox Wars against France 1712–1733); allied with the Sauk from 1735 on the upper Mississippi (Dubuque lead mines); Kansas 1846; repurchased land at Tama, Iowa 1857.

polities.name: Sauk
polities.note: Saginaw Bay (Michigan) before c.1650; Green Bay area 1650–1735; Rock River–Mississippi confluence (Saukenuk) c.1750–1831 in alliance with the Meskwaki; Black Hawk War 1832; Iowa, Kansas (1846) and Indian Territory (1869).

polities.name: Kickapoo
polities.note: First recorded in SW Wisconsin c.1650; central Illinois and Wabash from c.1700; ceded Illinois 1819; Missouri, Kansas (1832); bands in Coahuila (Nacimiento) from 1850s and Indian Territory.

polities.name: Illinois Confederation
polities.note: Confederation of c.12 Algonquian groups (Kaskaskia, Peoria, Cahokia, Michigamea, Tamaroa...) across the Illinois country; Grand Village at Starved Rock 1670s–1691, Peoria (Pimitoui) 1691–1700, then Kaskaskia; collapsed by war and disease; removed to Kansas 1832 (later Peoria Tribe of Indian Territory).

polities.name: Miami
polities.note: Pre-1650 homeland probably northern Indiana/NE Illinois; refugees in Wisconsin in the 1650s–70s, Chicago and St Joseph River in the 1680s, then Kekionga (Fort Wayne) and the Wabash (Wea, Piankashaw) c.1700–1794; reduced by the 1795 Greenville and later treaties; removed to Kansas 1846 (Indian Territory 1873), with an Indiana remnant.

polities.name: Shawnee
polities.note: Middle Ohio valley (probably Fort Ancient descendants) before the Beaver Wars; dispersed c.1670–1725 (Savannah River, Cumberland, Pennsylvania); regrouped in Ohio (Lower Shawnee Town, then Scioto and Chillicothe towns) until Greenville 1795; Wapakoneta, Missouri, Kansas (1831) and Indian Territory (1869).

polities.name: Western Confederacy
polities.note: Alliance of Shawnee, Miami, Lenape, Wyandot, Odawa, Ojibwe, Potawatomi and others defending the Ohio boundary; defeated at Fallen Timbers 1794; Treaty of Greenville 1795.

polities.name: Tecumseh's Confederacy
polities.note: Pan-tribal confederacy led by Tecumseh and Tenskwatawa; Prophetstown burned 1811 (Tippecanoe); ended with Tecumseh's death at the Thames 1813.

polities.name: Dakota
polities.note: Eastern bands of the Oceti Sakowin; around Mille Lacs until Ojibwe expansion c.1736, then the Minnesota River and Mississippi; ceded most land 1851; reservation strip on the Minnesota River 1851–1862; after the 1862 war exiled to Crow Creek, Santee (Nebraska) and Lake Traverse.

polities.name: Lakota
polities.note: Western division of the Oceti Sakowin. On the prairies of western Minnesota before c.1700; crossed the Missouri during the 18th c.; took the Black Hills c.1776; dominant northern plains power by 1850 (Fort Laramie treaties 1851, 1868; Powder River). Black Hills seized 1877; Great Sioux Reservation split into six reservations 1889.

polities.name: Yankton and Yanktonai
polities.note: Middle division of the Oceti Sakowin; in central Minnesota before c.1700, then the James and upper Minnesota valleys and the Missouri; Yankton ceded land 1858 for the Yankton reservation; Yanktonai at Standing Rock, Crow Creek and Fort Peck.

polities.name: Assiniboine
polities.note: Split from the Yanktonai by c.1640; Lake of the Woods–Lake Winnipeg region, then moved west with the Cree (Iron Confederacy) onto the Assiniboine, Souris, Qu'Appelle and upper Missouri; Stoney Nakoda in the Alberta foothills; reservations at Fort Belknap and Fort Peck and Canadian reserves after 1870s.

polities.name: Eastern Cree
polities.note: Hunting bands of the Hudson Bay lowlands, James Bay and Eeyou Istchee; trading partners of the Hudson's Bay Company from 1670 (Moose Factory, York Factory); no central government.

polities.name: Western Cree
polities.note: Woods Cree of the Saskatchewan lowlands and Lake Winnipeg region expanded west with the fur trade after 1690 (Lesser Slave Lake by 1760, Peace River boundary with the Dane-zaa); Plains Cree onto the parkland and plains from c.1740; Treaties 4 and 6 (1874, 1876); North-West Rebellion 1885.

polities.name: Iron Confederacy
polities.note: Alliance of Plains Cree, Assiniboine, Stoney, Saulteaux and Métis controlling trade to HBC posts (peak 1800–1850); weakened by bison decline after 1850; broke apart with the treaties and the 1885 resistance. Overlaps member territories.

polities.name: Red River Provisional Government
polities.note: Métis-led government under Louis Riel at the Red River Settlement (Dec 1869–Aug 1870) pending transfer of Rupert's Land; led to the Manitoba Act.

polities.name: Provisional Government of Saskatchewan
polities.note: Métis government of Riel and Dumont, March–May 1885, ended at the Battle of Batoche.

polities.name: Mandan
polities.note: Fortified earth-lodge towns on the Missouri around the Heart River; devastated by smallpox 1781; moved to the Knife River near the Hidatsa (Mitutanka) c.1787; 1837 epidemic; Like-a-Fishhook with Hidatsa and Arikara 1845; Fort Berthold Reservation 1870.

polities.name: Hidatsa
polities.note: Earth-lodge villages at the mouth of the Knife River; hunting range west to the Yellowstone; Like-a-Fishhook 1845, Fort Berthold Reservation 1870 (Three Affiliated Tribes).

polities.name: Arikara
polities.note: Caddoan earth-lodge towns on the Missouri in central South Dakota; reduced by smallpox in the 1780s and moved north; joined the Mandan and Hidatsa at Like-a-Fishhook 1862.

polities.name: Cheyenne
polities.note: Upper Mississippi/Minnesota River before c.1680; earth-lodge villages on the Sheyenne River (ND) c.1680–1770; Black Hills and plains nomads after 1770; split into Northern (Powder/Tongue rivers) and Southern (Arkansas, Bent's Fort) branches 1830s; reservations in Indian Territory 1869 and Montana 1884.

polities.name: Arapaho
polities.note: Earlier farming people of the Red River of the North/Minnesota region; plains nomads west of the Missouri by the 18th c.; held the Platte–Arkansas front range country (Fort Laramie 1851); Southern Arapaho to Indian Territory 1869, Northern to Wind River 1878.

polities.name: Pawnee
polities.note: Caddoan confederacy of four bands (Skidi, Chawi, Kitkahahki, Pitahawirata) in earth-lodge towns on the Platte, Loup and Republican rivers; ceded land 1833–1857; Genoa reservation 1857; removed to Indian Territory 1875.

polities.name: Omaha
polities.note: Dhegiha Siouan nation on the Missouri in NE Nebraska from c.1700 (Big Village c.1775–1845); ceded land 1854; Omaha Reservation at Macy.

polities.name: Ponca
polities.note: Dhegiha Siouan nation at the mouth of the Niobrara; forced removal to Indian Territory 1877 (Ponca Trail of Tears); some returned to Nebraska.

polities.name: Otoe-Missouria
polities.note: Chiwere Siouan peoples: Missouria on the Missouri (Gumbo Point) and Otoe on the lower Platte; Missouria joined the Otoe after 1798; Big Blue reservation 1855; Indian Territory 1881.

polities.name: Ioway
polities.note: Chiwere Siouan descendants of the Oneota of NE Iowa/SE Minnesota; spread across Iowa in the 18th c.; ceded lands 1824–1838; Great Nemaha reservation 1836; part moved to Indian Territory 1883.

polities.name: Kansa
polities.note: Dhegiha Siouan nation of the Kansas River valley; ceded most land 1825; Council Grove reservation 1846; Indian Territory 1873.

polities.name: Osage
polities.note: Dhegiha Siouan nation of the Osage River; dominant power between the Missouri and Red rivers c.1700–1800 (trade with French and Spanish); ceded Missouri and Arkansas lands 1808–1825; Kansas reserve 1825–1870; Osage Reservation (Pawhuska) in Indian Territory from 1872.

polities.name: Quapaw
polities.note: Dhegiha Siouan towns near the Arkansas–Mississippi confluence (met by Marquette 1673), allies of the French at Arkansas Post; ceded land 1818 and 1824; Indian Territory reserve from 1833.

polities.name: Cherokee Nation
polities.note: Southern Appalachian towns (Lower, Middle, Valley, Overhill); successive cessions 1721–1819; constitutional republic with capital New Echota 1825; removed 1838–39 (Trail of Tears) to Indian Territory (Tahlequah); Cherokee Outlet sold 1893; Eastern Band remained in North Carolina.

polities.name: Muscogee Confederacy
polities.note: Coalesced in the later 17th c. from Mississippian successor towns on the Coosa, Tallapoosa and Chattahoochee (Upper and Lower towns; Coweta and Tuckabatchee leading). Lost the Oconee lands 1790, half its territory at Fort Jackson 1814, the rest 1825–1832; removed 1836 to Indian Territory (Okmulgee capital 1867).

polities.name: Choctaw Nation
polities.note: Formed in the 17th c. from Plaquemine/Mississippian remnants in east-central Mississippi; three districts; French allies; cessions 1801–1820 (Doak's Stand); removed after Dancing Rabbit Creek 1830 to Indian Territory (Doaksville, Tuskahoma).

polities.name: Chickasaw Nation
polities.note: Mississippian chiefdom of Chicaza met by de Soto 1540–41 in NE Mississippi; British allies and slave-raiders in the 18th c.; western Tennessee/Kentucky sold 1818; Pontotoc cession 1832; Indian Territory from 1837 (Tishomingo capital 1856).

polities.name: Seminole
polities.note: Creek emigrants and Florida remnants forming a separate people from c.1750; Moultrie Creek reservation 1823; Second Seminole War 1835–42; Billy Bowlegs' band in SW Florida until 1858; Florida remnant in the Everglades/Big Cypress thereafter.

polities.name: Seminole Nation (Indian Territory)
polities.note: Removed Seminoles given their own territory separate from the Creek Nation 1856; reduced by the 1866 treaty.

polities.name: Natchez
polities.note: Last functioning Mississippian chiefdom (Great Sun); Emerald Mound centre before the Grand Village (c.1682); destroyed by France 1729–31; survivors joined the Chickasaw, Creek and Cherokee.

polities.name: Coosa
polities.note: Paramount chiefdom of seven or more chiefdoms (c.50,000 people) stretching ~400 miles along the Appalachians from eastern Tennessee to central Alabama; visited by de Soto 1540 and de Luna 1560; core abandoned by c.1600.

polities.name: Cofitachequi
polities.note: Paramount chiefdom of the Wateree valley (c.75,000 km2 in 1540) with influence to the NC Piedmont and Pee Dee; capital Talimeco (Adamson) c.1300–1450 then Canosi (Mulberry); diminished by epidemic and de Soto (1540); last mentioned 1670.

polities.name: Joara
polities.note: Mississippian chiefdom of the upper Catawba valley; Spanish Fort San Juan built there by Pardo 1567, destroyed 1568.

polities.name: Ocute
polities.note: Mississippian chiefdom of the Oconee valley, rival of Cofitachequi; visited by de Soto 1540 and Spanish expeditions 1597; dissolved in the early 17th c.

polities.name: Tascalusa
polities.note: Paramount chiefdom on the Alabama River whose ruler fought de Soto at Mabila (1540); fragmented afterwards.

polities.name: Moundville
polities.note: Major Black Warrior River paramount centre in decline after 1350; abandoned as a political seat by c.1450.

polities.name: Casqui
polities.note: Mississippian chiefdom on the St Francis River (NE Arkansas) visited by de Soto 1541; gone by the 17th c.

polities.name: Pacaha
polities.note: Mississippian chiefdom on the Mississippi in NE Arkansas, rival of Casqui, visited by de Soto 1541.

polities.name: Apalachee
polities.note: Mississippian chiefdom between the Aucilla and Ochlockonee rivers (Lake Jackson then Anhaica); Spanish mission province from 1633 (San Luis de Talimali); destroyed by Carolina–Creek raids 1704.

polities.name: Timucua chiefdoms
polities.note: Some 35 chiefdoms (Saturiwa, Utina, Potano, Yustaga, Mocama...) of north and central Florida and SE Georgia; Spanish mission province from 1595; revolt 1656; devastated by raids 1702–1706; survivors at St Augustine until 1763.

polities.name: Calusa
polities.note: Complex fisher-forager kingdom of SW Florida (Charlotte Harbor to Marco Island, inland to Lake Okeechobee) with influence over the Mayaimi, Tequesta, Jaega and Ais; resisted Spain; broken by slave raids after 1702; last survivors to Cuba 1763.

polities.name: Tequesta
polities.note: Chiefdom of the Biscayne Bay region, under Calusa influence; remnants removed to Cuba 1763.

polities.name: Ais
polities.note: Chiefdom on the Indian River lagoon of Florida's Atlantic coast (Jaega to the south); disappeared mid-18th c.

polities.name: Guale
polities.note: Chiefdoms of the Georgia coast; Spanish mission province from 1587 (revolt 1597); withdrew south under Carolina raids 1680–1702.

polities.name: Yamasee
polities.note: Multi-ethnic people in Spanish Guale then (from 1684) near Port Royal, South Carolina, as English allies; Yamasee War 1715–17 ended with flight to Florida.

polities.name: Westo
polities.note: Slave-raiding people (probably Erie refugees) on the Savannah River; destroyed in the Westo War 1680–82.

polities.name: Catawba
polities.note: Siouan coalescent nation of the Catawba valley (successor of Piedmont groups); 15-mile-square reservation from 1763; ceded 1840, small reservation after.

polities.name: Tunica
polities.note: Lower Mississippi valley people of the Yazoo basin; moved south to Angola (1706) and Marksville, Louisiana (c.1780s).

polities.name: Houma
polities.note: Recorded 1682 near the Red–Mississippi confluence; moved south to Bayou St John, Ascension and the Terrebonne bayous in the 18th c.

polities.name: Chitimacha
polities.note: Chiefdom of the Atchafalaya basin and Bayou Teche; war with France 1706–1718; small Charenton reservation afterwards.

polities.name: Atakapa
polities.note: Bands of SW Louisiana and SE Texas coast; absorbed into Creole and neighbouring communities by mid-19th c.

polities.name: Karankawa
polities.note: Bands of the Texas coast from Galveston Bay to Corpus Christi; encountered La Salle (1685); destroyed by Texan settlers by 1858.

polities.name: Hasinai Confederacy
polities.note: Caddo confederacy of the Neches and Angelina valleys (the 'Tejas'); Spanish missions 1690 and 1716; removed to the Brazos reservation 1855 and to Indian Territory (Anadarko) 1859.

polities.name: Kadohadacho Confederacy
polities.note: Caddo confederacy of the Great Bend of the Red River (incl. the Natchitoches group downriver); moved to Caddo Lake c.1790s; sold its land to the US 1835 and joined the Hasinai.

polities.name: Tonkawa
polities.note: Bison hunters of central Texas (moved south from the plains by the 17th c.); allied with Texas; Brazos reservation, then Indian Territory 1859 and Tonkawa, Oklahoma 1885.

polities.name: Republic of West Florida
aliases: Free and Independent State of West Florida
polities.note: Short-lived republic (Sept–Dec 1810) in the Baton Rouge district of Spanish West Florida, annexed by the United States.

polities.name: State of Franklin
polities.note: Unrecognised state in what is now NE Tennessee, functioning 1784–1788 before reverting to North Carolina.

polities.name: Republic of Texas
polities.note: Independent from Mexico 1836 until US annexation 1845; claimed to the Rio Grande (incl. eastern New Mexico) but effective control limited to east and central Texas below Comancheria; capitals Columbia, Houston, Austin.

polities.name: Wichita Confederacy
polities.note: Caddoan grass-house towns of central Kansas (Quivira, visited by Coronado 1541); moved south to northern Oklahoma c.1700 and the Red River (Taovaya 'Spanish Fort' towns) by 1757; Brazos and Wichita Mountains in the early 19th c.; Wichita-Caddo reservation at Anadarko from 1859.

polities.name: Comanche
polities.note: Separated from the Eastern Shoshone c.1700 and moved onto the southern plains (first Spanish report 1706); drove the Apache off the plains; Comanchería at its height c.1750–1850 (NW Texas, E New Mexico, SE Colorado, SW Kansas, W Oklahoma) with raids deep into Mexico; Medicine Lodge 1867; last band surrendered 1875 (Fort Sill reservation).

polities.name: Kiowa
polities.note: Upper Missouri/western Montana before c.1650; Black Hills with the Crow c.1650–1780; driven south by the Lakota and Cheyenne to the Arkansas and Red River drainages; alliance with the Comanche 1790; Medicine Lodge 1867; reservation (shared with Comanche and Plains Apache) after 1875.

polities.name: Plains Apache
polities.note: Apachean bison hunters of the western plains (Querechos and Teyas met by Coronado 1541; Dismal River culture); farming rancherías at El Cuartelejo; pushed off the plains by the Comanche and Ute after c.1720, survivors forming the Lipan, Jicarilla and Kiowa-Apache.

polities.name: Lipan Apache
polities.note: Southernmost plains Apache, pushed south by the Comanche onto the Edwards Plateau and south Texas (San Sabá mission 1757); into Coahuila after 1850; largely destroyed by US and Mexican campaigns by the 1880s.

polities.name: Mescalero Apache
polities.note: Apache of SE New Mexico and West Texas (Sacramento and Guadalupe Mountains, Big Bend); interned at Bosque Redondo 1862–65; Mescalero reservation from 1873.

polities.name: Jicarilla Apache
polities.note: Apache of NE New Mexico and SE Colorado, partly farming; under Comanche pressure in the 18th c.; reservation at Dulce from 1887.

polities.name: Chiricahua Apache
polities.note: Bands of SE Arizona, SW New Mexico and northern Sonora/Chihuahua (Cochise, Mangas Coloradas, Geronimo); Chiricahua reservation 1872–76; surrendered 1886 and held as prisoners of war.

polities.name: Western Apache
polities.note: Bands of east-central Arizona (Mogollon Rim, White Mountains, Tonto Basin); Fort Apache and San Carlos reservations from 1871–72.

polities.name: Navajo
polities.note: Apachean people of Dinétah (upper San Juan) by c.1500; spread west after the Pueblo Revolt; Long Walk to Bosque Redondo 1864–68; treaty reservation 1868, enlarged 1878–1884.

polities.name: Hopi
polities.note: Independent village theocracies of the three mesas; Spanish missions 1629–1680; never re-subjugated after the Pueblo Revolt; Hopi reservation 1882.

polities.name: Zuni
polities.note: Six towns of Cíbola (Hawikuh first stormed by Coronado 1540) consolidated at Halona after 1692.

polities.name: Acoma Pueblo
polities.note: Western Keresan mesa-top pueblo; Acoma Massacre 1599.

polities.name: Keres Pueblos
polities.note: Independent Eastern Keresan pueblos on the Rio Grande and Jemez rivers.

polities.name: Tewa Pueblos
polities.note: Northern Rio Grande pueblos; Popé of Ohkay Owingeh led the 1680 revolt.

polities.name: Northern Tiwa Pueblos
polities.note: Taos and Picuris, the northernmost pueblos and trade fair centres with plains peoples.

polities.name: Southern Tiwa Pueblos
polities.note: Tiguex province (c.12 towns) attacked by Coronado 1540–41; many withdrew to Ysleta del Sur (El Paso) after 1680; Isleta and Sandia reoccupied.

polities.name: Jemez Pueblo
polities.note: Towa-speaking pueblos of the Jemez canyons, consolidated at Walatowa after 1700.

polities.name: Pecos Pueblo
polities.note: Fortified Towa gateway town between the pueblos and the plains; declined in the 18th c.; last residents moved to Jemez 1838.

polities.name: Piro Pueblos
polities.note: Southern Rio Grande pueblos; withdrew with the Spanish to the El Paso area in 1680–81.

polities.name: Salinas Pueblos
polities.note: Tompiro and Tiwa pueblos east of the Manzano Mountains; abandoned in the 1670s through drought, famine and Apache raids.

polities.name: Pueblo Revolt confederacy
polities.note: Coordinated rising of the pueblos under Popé expelled Spain from New Mexico 1680; independent until Vargas' reconquest 1692. Overlaps member pueblos.

polities.name: Ute
polities.note: Numic bands of Utah and western Colorado; mounted raiders/traders with New Mexico from the 17th c.; Walker and Black Hawk wars 1853–72; Colorado reservation 1868 lost after 1879 (Meeker); Uintah-Ouray (Utah) and Southern Ute reservations.

polities.name: Southern Paiute
polities.note: Numic farming-foraging bands of southern Nevada, SW Utah and N Arizona (incl. the Chemehuevi); heavily raided for slaves by Ute and New Mexicans; small reservations from 1870s.

polities.name: Western Shoshone
polities.note: Numic bands of central/eastern Nevada and western Utah (Goshute), Death Valley (Timbisha); Treaty of Ruby Valley 1863.

polities.name: Northern Shoshone and Bannock
polities.note: Snake River plain and Salmon River (Lemhi, Sacagawea's people); mounted bison hunters; Bannock War 1878; Fort Hall reservation 1868.

polities.name: Eastern Shoshone
polities.note: Mounted Shoshone dominated the NW plains (into Alberta and Montana) c.1500–1750 before smallpox and Blackfoot guns pushed them back to the Wind River and Green River; the Comanche separated c.1700; Wind River reservation 1868 (Washakie).

polities.name: Crow
polities.note: Split from the Hidatsa c.1600 and occupied the Yellowstone, Bighorn and Powder river basins (Mountain and River Crow); Fort Laramie 1851 territory; reservation 1868, reduced 1882 and 1891.

polities.name: Blackfoot Confederacy
polities.note: Siksika, Kainai and Piikani of the NW plains; expanded south and west at Shoshone expense c.1730–1800 with horses and guns; dominant from the North Saskatchewan to the Missouri headwaters; Lame Bull Treaty 1855, Blackfeet Reservation (Montana) and Treaty 7 reserves (1877).

polities.name: Gros Ventre
polities.note: Algonquian plains people allied with the Blackfoot, between the Saskatchewan and Missouri; Fort Belknap reservation 1888.

polities.name: Tsuut'ina
polities.note: Dene people who separated from the Dane-zaa and joined the Blackfoot alliance on the upper Saskatchewan; Treaty 7 reserve 1877.

polities.name: Jumano
polities.note: Farming and trading people of La Junta de los Ríos and the southern plains, with a long-distance trade network; absorbed by Apache and Spanish missions by 1750.

polities.name: State of Deseret
polities.note: Provisional Mormon state that governed the Great Salt Lake and Utah valley settlements 1849–1851 (claimed far larger area) until Utah Territory took effect; extent is the effectively settled corridor.

polities.name: Yaqui
polities.note: Farming nation of the lower Río Yaqui; repelled Spanish expeditions (1533, 1609–10), accepted Jesuit missions 1617 while keeping self-rule in eight pueblos; revolts 1740 and 1825–33 (Banderas); effectively autonomous under Cajeme until 1887, then subjected and deported.

polities.name: Mayo
polities.note: Cahitan farmers of the Mayo and Fuerte rivers; Jesuit missions from 1614; joined Yaqui risings in the 18th–19th c.

polities.name: Seri
polities.note: Hunter-fisher bands of the Sonoran Gulf coast and Tiburón Island; resisted missionisation and Spanish/Mexican campaigns throughout.

polities.name: Tohono O'odham
polities.note: Desert O'odham of the Papaguería (southern Arizona and NW Sonora); Pimería Alta missions from 1687 (Kino); divided by the Gadsden Purchase 1854; San Xavier reservation 1874.

polities.name: Akimel O'odham
polities.note: Irrigation farmers of the middle Gila River (with Maricopa allies from the 18th c.); Upper Pima of the Santa Cruz and San Pedro under Pimería Alta missions; Gila River reservation 1859.

polities.name: Opata
polities.note: Densely settled river-valley statelets of the Sonora, Moctezuma and Bavispe valleys (described by Cabeza de Vaca and Coronado's party); mission towns from the 1640s, Spanish allies against the Apache; assimilated after independence.

polities.name: Rarámuri
polities.note: Uto-Aztecan people of the Sierra Madre Occidental (Chihuahua); revolts 1648–1697; withdrew into the barrancas, largely self-governing.

polities.name: Tepehuán
polities.note: Northern and Southern Tepehuán of the Durango sierra; great revolt 1616–1620.

polities.name: Acaxee and Xixime
polities.note: Mountain peoples of the Sierra Madre between Durango and Sinaloa; revolted 1601; subdued by 1610.

polities.name: Tahue chiefdoms
polities.note: Coastal Sinaloa chiefdoms (Tahue of Culiacán, Totorame of Chiametla) conquered by Nuño de Guzmán 1530–31.

polities.name: Conchos
polities.note: Rancherías along the Río Conchos (Chihuahua); revolts 1644–1684; absorbed into the mission/hacienda population by the mid-18th c.

polities.name: Coahuiltecan bands

seat.name: San Juan Bautista del Río Grande

polities.note: Hundreds of small hunter-gatherer bands of south Texas and NE Mexico, gathered into missions (San Antonio, Río Grande) in the 18th c.; disappeared as distinct groups by c.1800.

polities.name: Guachichil
polities.note: Largest Chichimec nation of the central plateau (San Luis Potosí, Zacatecas); fought the Chichimeca War 1550–1590; pacified by settlement with Tlaxcalans c.1591–1600.

polities.name: Zacateco
polities.note: Chichimec nation of Zacatecas and NE Durango; subdued after the Chichimeca War.

polities.name: Caxcan
polities.note: Nahua-speaking town-chiefdoms of southern Zacatecas/northern Jalisco; led the Mixtón War 1540–42 against New Spain.

polities.name: Kingdom of Nayar
polities.note: Cora polity in the Sierra del Nayar ruled by the Tonati, a refuge independent of New Spain for two centuries; Spanish expedition failed 1716, conquered 1722.

polities.name: Wixárika
polities.note: Self-governing Huichol communities of the Sierra Madre east of the Cora; nominally under Spain after 1722.

polities.name: Cochimí
polities.note: Hunter-gatherer bands of central Baja California; Jesuit missions from 1697 (Loreto) devastated the population by the early 19th c.

polities.name: Guaycura and Pericú
polities.note: Peoples of the southern Baja California peninsula; Pericú revolt 1734–37; extinct as groups by c.1800.

polities.name: Kumeyaay
polities.note: Bands of the San Diego region and northern Baja California; burned Mission San Diego 1775; divided by the 1848 border.

polities.name: Quechan
polities.note: Controlled the Colorado–Gila confluence crossing; destroyed the Spanish missions there in the 1781 Yuma revolt; Fort Yuma reservation 1884.

polities.name: Mohave
polities.note: Floodplain farmers of the lower Colorado River; Colorado River and Fort Mojave reservations from 1865.

polities.name: Cocopah
polities.note: Yuman farmers of the Colorado River delta, divided by the 1848/1854 border.

polities.name: Yavapai
polities.note: Yuman bands of central and western Arizona; removed to San Carlos 1875 (Exodus), returning in the 1900s.

polities.name: Pai
polities.note: Upland Yuman bands of NW Arizona and the Grand Canyon (Havasupai); Hualapai War 1866–70; reservations 1880–83.

polities.name: Chumash
polities.note: Maritime chiefdoms of the Santa Barbara Channel and islands (tomol plank-canoe trade, hereditary wots); missions from 1772; revolt 1824.

polities.name: Tongva
polities.note: Village polities of the Los Angeles basin and southern Channel Islands; Mission San Gabriel 1771.

polities.name: Payómkawichum
polities.note: Village groups of northern San Diego and southern Orange counties.

polities.name: Cahuilla
polities.note: Clan-based groups of the Coachella valley and San Jacinto mountains; outside the mission system; reservations from 1876.

polities.name: Yokuts
polities.note: Some 50 tribelets of the San Joaquin valley and Sierra foothills; largely outside Spanish control; Mariposa War 1850–51; Tule River reservation 1873.

polities.name: Miwok
polities.note: Tribelets of the Sierra foothills and Delta (Coast and Lake Miwok to the west); devastated in the Gold Rush.

polities.name: Ohlone
polities.note: About 50 tribelets around San Francisco and Monterey bays; absorbed into seven missions 1770–1800.

polities.name: Pomo
polities.note: Tribelets of the Russian River, Clear Lake and Mendocino coast; Fort Ross (Russian) on the southern edge 1812–1841; Bloody Island massacre 1850.

polities.name: Wintun
polities.note: Wintu, Nomlaki and Patwin tribelets of the western Sacramento valley.

polities.name: Maidu
polities.note: Village communities of the northern Sierra Nevada and eastern Sacramento valley.

polities.name: Northwestern California peoples
polities.note: Town-based Yurok, Karuk, Hupa, Tolowa and Wiyot of the Klamath–Trinity rivers and coast; Hoopa Valley reservation 1864.

polities.name: Shasta
polities.note: Shasta of the Klamath and Shasta rivers (Rogue River Wars 1850s).

polities.name: Achomawi
polities.note: Eleven Pit River bands of NE California.

polities.name: Modoc
polities.note: Tule Lake and Lost River basin; Klamath reservation 1864; Modoc War 1872–73, survivors exiled to Indian Territory.

polities.name: Klamath
polities.note: Upper Klamath Lake and Klamath Marsh; Klamath reservation 1864.

polities.name: Washoe
polities.note: Hokan-speaking bands around Lake Tahoe and the Carson valley.

polities.name: Northern Paiute
polities.note: Numic bands of western Nevada, eastern Oregon and NE California; Pyramid Lake War 1860; Snake War 1864–68; Pyramid Lake and Malheur reservations.

polities.name: Nez Perce
polities.note: Plateau nation of the Clearwater, Snake and Wallowa valleys; 1855 treaty reservation of 7.5 million acres reduced 90% in 1863; Nez Perce War 1877 (Chief Joseph's band exiled to Indian Territory, later Colville).

polities.name: Cayuse, Umatilla and Walla Walla
polities.note: Horse-rich Sahaptin/Cayuse peoples of the Walla Walla and Umatilla valleys; Cayuse War 1847–55; Umatilla reservation 1855.

polities.name: Yakama
polities.note: Sahaptin bands of the Yakima valley; Kamiakin's confederacy in the Yakima War 1855–58; Yakama reservation 1855.

polities.name: Palouse
polities.note: Sahaptin people of the lower Snake and Palouse rivers; refused reservation life; dispersed after 1877–80.

polities.name: Wasco-Wishram
polities.note: Upper Chinookan traders at The Dalles–Celilo Falls fishery, the great trade mart of the Columbia; Warm Springs reservation 1855.

polities.name: Spokane
polities.note: Interior Salish bands of the Spokane River; Spokane reservation 1881.

polities.name: Schitsu'umsh
polities.note: Interior Salish of Lake Coeur d'Alene; reservation 1873.

polities.name: Bitterroot Salish and Pend d'Oreille
polities.note: Interior Salish of the Bitterroot, Clark Fork and Flathead Lake (Pend d'Oreille, Kalispel); crossed to the plains for bison; Hellgate Treaty 1855 created the Flathead (Jocko) reservation; Bitterroot band removed 1891.

polities.name: Ktunaxa
polities.note: Upper Columbia and Kootenay River bands of SE British Columbia, N Idaho and NW Montana.

polities.name: Plateau Salish of the upper Columbia
polities.note: Interior Salish bands of the Okanagan, Arrow Lakes and upper Columbia (Kettle Falls fishery); Colville reservation 1872.

polities.name: Secwépemc
polities.note: Interior Salish of the Thompson and upper Fraser rivers; reserves after 1862.

polities.name: Nlaka'pamux and St'át'imc
polities.note: Interior Salish of the Fraser Canyon and Thompson River (Nlaka'pamux) and the Lillooet country (St'át'imc); Fraser Canyon War 1858.

polities.name: Tsilhqot'in
polities.note: Dene nation of the Chilcotin plateau; Chilcotin War 1864.

polities.name: Dakelh
polities.note: Dene clans of the upper Fraser and Nechako (incl. Wet'suwet'en of the Bulkley); NWC/HBC New Caledonia posts from 1806.

polities.name: Chinookan peoples
polities.note: Trading towns of the lower Columbia (Comcomly at Chinook Point); population collapsed in the 1830 malaria epidemics; no reservation until the 20th c.

polities.name: Kalapuya
polities.note: Bands of the Willamette valley; removed to the Grand Ronde reservation 1855–56.

polities.name: Oregon Coast and Rogue River peoples
polities.note: Village peoples of the Oregon coast and Rogue/Umpqua valleys; Rogue River Wars 1855–56 ended with removal to the Siletz and Grand Ronde reservations.

polities.name: Coast Salish of Puget Sound
polities.note: Village-based Lushootseed peoples (Chief Seattle's Suquamish-Duwamish); Medicine Creek and Point Elliott treaties 1854–55; Puget Sound War 1855–56.

polities.name: Coast Salish of the Georgia Strait
polities.note: Halkomelem, Squamish and Straits Salish towns of the lower Fraser, Georgia Strait and SE Vancouver Island; Douglas treaties 1850–54; reserves after.

polities.name: Makah
polities.note: Whaling people of Cape Flattery (Ozette); Treaty of Neah Bay 1855.

polities.name: Olympic coast peoples
polities.note: Quinault, Quileute, Hoh and Chehalis villages of the Pacific coast of Washington; Quinault reservation 1855.

polities.name: Nuu-chah-nulth
polities.note: Chiefdoms of western Vancouver Island; Mowachaht chief Maquinna dominated the maritime fur trade at Nootka Sound (Nootka Crisis 1789–94).

polities.name: Kwakwaka'wakw
polities.note: Village chiefdoms of NE Vancouver Island and Queen Charlotte Strait; Fort Rupert (1849) became the main village.

polities.name: Heiltsuk
polities.note: Central coast chiefdoms (incl. Wuikinuxv of Rivers Inlet).

polities.name: Nuxalk
polities.note: Salishan people of the Bella Coola valley, at the end of the grease trail to the interior.

polities.name: Haisla
polities.note: Wakashan people of Douglas Channel and the Kitlope.

polities.name: Tsimshian
polities.note: Nine allied tribes of the lower Skeena and Prince Rupert harbour; Chief Legaic controlled the Skeena trade; moved to Fort Simpson (Lax Kw'alaams) after 1834.

polities.name: Nisga'a
polities.note: House-based chiefdoms of the Nass River valley.

polities.name: Gitxsan
polities.note: House-based chiefdoms of the upper Skeena.

polities.name: Haida
polities.note: Town chiefdoms of Haida Gwaii; the Kaigani Haida settled southern Prince of Wales Island (Alaska) c.1700; smallpox 1862 reduced survivors to Masset and Skidegate.

polities.name: Tlingit
polities.note: Clan-based kwáans of the Alaska panhandle (Sitka, Chilkat, Stikine, Yakutat...); destroyed Russian Sitka 1802, lost it 1804; controlled interior trade passes; US sovereignty from 1867.

polities.name: Denesuline
polities.note: Dene caribou hunters of the barren-ground edge between Great Slave Lake, Lake Athabasca and Hudson Bay (incl. the Yellowknives); HBC trade via Churchill (1717) and Fort Chipewyan (1788); Treaties 8 and 10 (1899, 1906).

polities.name: Tłı̨chǫ
polities.note: Dene of the land between Great Slave and Great Bear lakes.

polities.name: Dehcho Dene
polities.note: Dene bands of the upper Mackenzie (Deh Cho), Liard and Hay rivers; NWC/HBC posts from 1804.

polities.name: Sahtu Dene
polities.note: Dene bands around Great Bear Lake and the lower-middle Mackenzie.

polities.name: Gwich'in
polities.note: Northernmost Dene, of the Porcupine, Peel and upper Yukon (Fort Yukon 1847).

polities.name: Tanana and Han Athabaskans
polities.note: Dene bands of the Tanana valley and the Yukon around Eagle and Dawson (Hän).

polities.name: Koyukon
polities.note: Dene of the middle Yukon and Koyukuk rivers; Russian post at Nulato 1838 (destroyed 1851).

polities.name: Lower Yukon–Kuskokwim Athabaskans
polities.note: Dene bands of the lower Yukon/Innoko and upper Kuskokwim.

polities.name: Ahtna
polities.note: Dene of the Copper River basin who controlled the native copper trade and repelled Russian expeditions (1794–1848).

polities.name: Dena'ina
polities.note: Only coastal Dene, around Cook Inlet; Russian redoubt at Kenai 1791.

polities.name: Tutchone
polities.note: Dene bands of the central and southern Yukon; Chilkat Tlingit destroyed HBC Fort Selkirk 1852 to protect their trade monopoly.

polities.name: Kaska
polities.note: Dene of the upper Liard basin.

polities.name: Tahltan
polities.note: Dene of the upper Stikine, trading partners of the Stikine Tlingit.

polities.name: Sekani
polities.note: Dene of the Finlay and Parsnip rivers (Rocky Mountain Trench).

polities.name: Dane-zaa
polities.note: Dene of the Peace River country; pushed upriver by the Cree (Peace Point boundary c.1781); Rocky Mountain Fort 1794.

polities.name: Iñupiat
polities.note: Some 25 nations (nunaqatigiit) of northern and NW Alaska, with trade fairs at Sheshalik and Nigliq; US sovereignty from 1867.

polities.name: Yup'ik
polities.note: Regional nations of the Yukon–Kuskokwim delta and Bristol Bay (Bow and Arrow Wars before c.1840); Russian posts from 1818.

polities.name: Alutiiq
polities.note: Kodiak archipelago, Alaska Peninsula and Prince William Sound (Chugach); conquered by Shelikhov at Awa'uq 1784 and subjected to Russian-American Company labour.

polities.name: Unangan
polities.note: Island villages of the Aleutian chain (Near Islands west of 180° omitted); subjugated by Russian promyshlenniki after the 1763–66 war; forced labour in the fur trade.

polities.name: Inuvialuit
polities.note: Several regional groups of the Mackenzie delta and Beaufort coast (beluga hunt at Kitigaaryuit); population collapse after 1890s epidemics.

polities.name: Inuinnait
polities.note: Inuit of Victoria Island and the Coronation Gulf, using native copper; little outside contact before 1910.

polities.name: Netsilingmiut
polities.note: Seal-hunting Inuit of Boothia, King William Island and the Back River.

polities.name: Iglulingmiut and Aivilingmiut
polities.note: Inuit of the Melville Peninsula, Iglulik and NW Hudson Bay; Aivilingmiut at Repulse Bay traded with whalers from the 1860s.

polities.name: Sallirmiut
polities.note: Isolated Dorset-descended people of Southampton, Coats and Walrus islands; extinct 1902–03.

polities.name: Kivallirmiut
polities.note: Inland caribou-hunting Inuit west of Hudson Bay (Kazan and Dubawnt rivers), trading at Churchill.

polities.name: Qikiqtaaluk Inuit
polities.note: Regional Inuit groups of Baffin Island; Frobisher's contacts 1576–78; Scottish and American whaling stations in Cumberland Sound from 1840.

polities.name: Nunavimmiut
polities.note: Inuit of the Ungava Peninsula and the east Hudson Bay coast; HBC Fort Chimo 1830.

polities.name: Labrador Inuit
polities.note: Labrador coast Inuit who seasonally reached the Strait of Belle Isle in the 16th–18th c.; Moravian mission at Nain 1771 (then Okak, Hopedale, Hebron); southern range lost after c.1770.

polities.name: Norse Greenland
polities.note: Norse colony (Western Settlement abandoned c.1350–1400); last written record 1408 (Hvalsey wedding); Eastern Settlement extinct by c.1450.

polities.name: Kalaallit
polities.note: Thule-descended Inuit of the West Greenland coast, spreading into the former Norse districts after c.1400; Danish-Norwegian mission and trading colonies from 1721 (Hans Egede, Godthåb 1728); Royal Greenland Trade monopoly from 1776.

polities.name: Tunumiit
polities.note: Isolated East Greenland Inuit (Ammassalik and SE coast); first European contact by Holm's umiak expedition 1884; Danish station 1894.

polities.name: Inughuit
polities.note: Northernmost people in the world, isolated in the Thule district c.1600s–1818 (contact with Ross); joined by Baffin Inuit migrants under Qitlaq c.1863.

gaps.area: Queen Elizabeth Islands and the high Arctic archipelago (Ellesmere interior, Devon, Bathurst, Melville, Parry islands)
gaps.note: Thule Inuit occupation ended c.1450–1600 with the Little Ice Age; no permanent polity thereafter (Inughuit hunting forays into Ellesmere only).

gaps.area: Greenland ice sheet interior and NE Greenland coast (north of Scoresby Sund)
gaps.note: Ice sheet uninhabited; small NE Greenland Inuit groups died out by the early 19th c. (none met by Clavering 1823 except a last band).

gaps.area: Kentucky and the middle Ohio valley interior ('Vacant Quarter' / hunting grounds)
gaps.note: Largely unsettled after Mississippian/Fort Ancient decline; contested hunting ground of Shawnee, Cherokee, Chickasaw and Haudenosaunee rather than a governed homeland.

gaps.area: Central Mississippi valley around the Ohio confluence (Vacant Quarter)
gaps.note: Depopulated after c.1450; no identifiable polity until Illinois, Quapaw and Chickasaw use.

gaps.area: Mojave and Colorado deserts / southern Sierra (Serrano, Kawaiisu, Tübatulabal, Mono, Panamint)
gaps.note: Small band societies not listed individually; thin coverage.

gaps.area: Central California coast (Salinan, Esselen) and Coast Miwok/Wappo pockets
gaps.note: Small tribelets not listed separately; absorbed into missions 1770s–1830s.

gaps.area: Bolsón de Mapimí and Chihuahuan desert interior
gaps.note: Refuge and raiding zone (Toboso, Cocoyome, later Apache and Comanche war trails) with no stable polity.
Many small hunter-gatherer bands (Coahuiltecan, Borrados, Janambre) only partly covered by the Coahuiltecan entry; Tamaulipas coast thin.

gaps.area: Eastern United States, Ontario and Quebec lowlands after European settlement
gaps.note: Native homelands shown here shrink to reservations; colonial and settler states (covered by the base dataset) fill the land.

gaps.area: Long Island, lower Connecticut coast, Delmarva interior, Carolina Piedmont Siouan peoples (Montaukett, Quiripi, Saponi, Tutelo, Occaneechi, Cheraw, Waxhaw, Santee, Cusabo)
gaps.note: Small nations not listed individually; partial coverage via neighbours.
